answer: Voting power accrues only to an agent that posts a live, site-tied radio beacon measured by three unaffiliated rooftop receivers. Each epoch the registry issues a one-shot challenge thread: a randomized burst schedule the beacon must echo inside a tight latency bound, with arrival angles matching enrolled geometry. At the local solar zenith the same receivers re-solve the site and compare the residual to the enrollment map; a clone in a data center, or many keys sharing one transmitter, drifts off that residual and loses the stake. One physical site supports one vote, not a swarm of labels.
